- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.30), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +3–4% above peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend (e.g., -0.40 → +0.10), model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 20% above 18d history mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if 18d history mean is > 10% above 30d forecast, adjust forecast to align with 18d mean for next 5 days.
- High sentiment volatility (±0.30+ swings) → reduce forecast smoothing; use 3-day moving average instead of 5-day for short-term correction.
